10.L109:
<n>109:2</n> Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
<n>109:3</n> Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
<n>109:4</n> Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
<n>109:5</n> Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
<n>109:6</n> Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
<n>109:7</n> De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
10.E109:
<n>109:2</n> The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.
<n>109:3</n> With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.
<n>109:4</n> The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.
<n>109:5</n> The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.
<n>109:6</n> He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.
<n>109:7</n> He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.
10.L100:
<n>100:1</n> Misericórdiam, et judícium * cantábo tibi, Dómine:
<n>100:2</n> Psallam, et intéllegam in via immaculáta, * quando vénies ad me.
<n>100:2</n> Perambulábam in innocéntia cordis mei, * in médio domus meæ.
<n>100:3</n> Non proponébam ante óculos meos rem injústam: * faciéntes prævaricatiónes odívi.
<n>100:4</n> Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum: * declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam.
<n>100:5</n> Detrahéntem secréto próximo suo, * hunc persequébar.
<n>100:5</n> Supérbo óculo, et insatiábili corde, * cum hoc non edébam.
<n>100:6</n> Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum: * ámbulans in via immaculáta, hic mihi ministrábat.
<n>100:7</n> Non habitábit in médio domus meæ qui facit supérbiam: * qui lóquitur iníqua, non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum.
<n>100:8</n> In matutíno interficiébam omnes peccatóres terræ: * ut dispérderem de civitáte Dómini omnes operántes iniquitátem.
10.L101:
<n>101:2</n> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<n>101:3</n> Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.
<n>101:3</n> In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.
<n>101:4</n> Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.
<n>101:5</n> Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
<n>101:6</n> A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
<n>101:7</n> Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
<n>101:8</n> Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
<n>101:9</n> Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me jurábant.
<n>101:10</n> Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.
<n>101:11</n> A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.
<n>101:12</n> Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.
<n>101:13</n> Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
<n>101:14</n> Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi ejus, quia venit tempus.
<n>101:15</n> Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides ejus: * et terræ ejus miserebúntur.
<n>101:16</n> Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
<n>101:17</n> Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.
<n>101:18</n> Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.
<n>101:19</n> Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:
<n>101:20</n> Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:
<n>101:21</n> Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:
<n>101:22</n> Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem ejus in Jerúsalem.
<n>101:23</n> In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.
<n>101:24</n> Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
<n>101:25</n> Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
<n>101:26</n> Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
<n>101:27</n> Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
<n>101:28</n> Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
<n>101:29</n> Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
10.L102:
<n>102:1</n> Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et ómnia, quæ intra me sunt, nómini sancto ejus.
<n>102:2</n> Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * et noli oblivísci omnes retributiónes ejus.
<n>102:3</n> Qui propitiátur ómnibus iniquitátibus tuis: * qui sanat omnes infirmitátes tuas.
<n>102:4</n> Qui rédimit de intéritu vitam tuam: * qui corónat te in misericórdia et miseratiónibus.
<n>102:5</n> Qui replet in bonis desidérium tuum: * renovábitur ut áquilæ juvéntus tua:
<n>102:6</n> Fáciens misericórdias Dóminus: * et judícium ómnibus injúriam patiéntibus.
<n>102:7</n> Notas fecit vias suas Móysi, * fíliis Israël voluntátes suas.
<n>102:8</n> Miserátor, et miséricors Dóminus: * longánimis, et multum miséricors.
<n>102:9</n> Non in perpétuum irascétur: * neque in ætérnum comminábitur.
<n>102:10</n> Non secúndum peccáta nostra fecit nobis: * neque secúndum iniquitátes nostras retríbuit nobis.
<n>102:11</n> Quóniam secúndum altitúdinem cæli a terra: * corroborávit misericórdiam suam super timéntes se.
<n>102:12</n> Quantum distat ortus ab occidénte: * longe fecit a nobis iniquitátes nostras.
<n>102:13</n> Quómodo miserétur pater filiórum, misértus est Dóminus timéntibus se: * quóniam ipse cognóvit figméntum nostrum.
<n>102:14</n> Recordátus est quóniam pulvis sumus: * homo, sicut fænum dies ejus, tamquam flos agri sic efflorébit.
<n>102:16</n> Quóniam spíritus pertransíbit in illo, et non subsístet: * et non cognóscet ámplius locum suum.
<n>102:17</n> Misericórdia autem Dómini ab ætérno, * et usque in ætérnum super timéntes eum.
<n>102:17</n> Et justítia illíus in fílios filiórum, * his qui servant testaméntum ejus:
<n>102:18</n> Et mémores sunt mandatórum ipsíus, * ad faciéndum ea.
<n>102:19</n> Dóminus in cælo parávit sedem suam: * et regnum ipsíus ómnibus dominábitur.
<n>102:20</n> Benedícite Dómino, omnes Ángeli ejus: * poténtes virtúte, faciéntes verbum illíus, ad audiéndam vocem sermónum ejus.
<n>102:21</n> Benedícite Dómino, omnes virtútes ejus: * minístri ejus, qui fácitis voluntátem ejus.
<n>102:22</n> Benedícite Dómino, ómnia ópera ejus: * in omni loco dominatiónis ejus, bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.
10.L103:
<n>103:1</n> Bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino: * Dómine, Deus meus, magnificátus es veheménter.
<n>103:1</n> Confessiónem, et decórem induísti: * amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto:
<n>103:2</n> Exténdens cælum sicut pellem: * qui tegis aquis superióra ejus.
<n>103:3</n> Qui ponis nubem ascénsum tuum: * qui ámbulas super pennas ventórum.
<n>103:4</n> Qui facis ángelos tuos, spíritus: * et minístros tuos ignem uréntem.
<n>103:5</n> Qui fundásti terram super stabilitátem suam: * non inclinábitur in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>103:6</n> Abýssus, sicut vestiméntum, amíctus ejus: * super montes stabunt aquæ.
<n>103:7</n> Ab increpatióne tua fúgient: * a voce tonítrui tui formidábunt.
<n>103:8</n> Ascéndunt montes: et descéndunt campi * in locum, quem fundásti eis.
<n>103:9</n> Términum posuísti, quem non transgrediéntur: * neque converténtur operíre terram.
<n>103:10</n> Qui emíttis fontes in convállibus: * inter médium móntium pertransíbunt aquæ.
<n>103:11</n> Potábunt omnes béstiæ agri: * exspectábunt ónagri in siti sua.
<n>103:12</n> Super ea vólucres cæli habitábunt: * de médio petrárum dabunt voces.
<n>103:13</n> Rigans montes de superióribus suis: * de fructu óperum tuórum satiábitur terra:
<n>103:14</n> Prodúcens fænum juméntis, * et herbam servitúti hóminum:
<n>103:14</n> Ut edúcas panem de terra: * et vinum lætíficet cor hóminis:
<n>103:15</n> Ut exhílaret fáciem in óleo: * et panis cor hóminis confírmet.
<n>103:16</n> Saturabúntur ligna campi, et cedri Líbani, quas plantávit: * illic pásseres nidificábunt.
<n>103:17</n> Heródii domus dux est eórum: * montes excélsi cervis: petra refúgium herináciis.
<n>103:19</n> Fecit lunam in témpora: * sol cognóvit occásum suum.
<n>103:20</n> Posuísti ténebras, et facta est nox: * in ipsa pertransíbunt omnes béstiæ silvæ.
<n>103:21</n> Cátuli leónum rugiéntes, ut rápiant, * et quærant a Deo escam sibi.
<n>103:22</n> Ortus est sol, et congregáti sunt: * et in cubílibus suis collocabúntur.
<n>103:23</n> Exíbit homo ad opus suum: * et ad operatiónem suam usque ad vésperum.
<n>103:24</n> Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti: impléta est terra possessióne tua.
<n>103:25</n> Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus: * illic reptília, quorum non est númerus.
<n>103:26</n> Animália pusílla cum magnis: * illic naves pertransíbunt.
<n>103:27</n> Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei: * ómnia a te exspéctant ut des illis escam in témpore.
<n>103:28</n> Dante te illis, cólligent: * aperiénte te manum tuam, ómnia implebúntur bonitáte.
<n>103:29</n> Averténte autem te fáciem, turbabúntur: * áuferes spíritum eórum, et defícient, et in púlverem suum reverténtur.
<n>103:30</n> Emíttes spíritum tuum, et creabúntur: * et renovábis fáciem terræ.
<n>103:31</n> Sit glória Dómini in sǽculum: * lætábitur Dóminus in opéribus suis:
<n>103:32</n> Qui réspicit terram, et facit eam trémere: * qui tangit montes, et fúmigant.
<n>103:33</n> Cantábo Dómino in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo, quámdiu sum.
<n>103:34</n> Jucúndum sit ei elóquium meum: * ego vero delectábor in Dómino.
<n>103:35</n> Defíciant peccatóres a terra, et iníqui ita ut non sint: * bénedic, ánima mea, Dómino.
10.L104:
<n>104:1</n> Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen ejus: * annuntiáte inter gentes ópera ejus.
<n>104:2</n> Cantáte ei, et psállite ei: * narráte ómnia mirabília ejus.
<n>104:3</n> Laudámini in nómine sancto ejus: * lætétur cor quæréntium Dóminum.
<n>104:4</n> Quǽrite Dóminum, et confirmámini: * quǽrite fáciem ejus semper.
<n>104:5</n> Mementóte mirabílium ejus, quæ fecit: * prodígia ejus, et judícia oris ejus.
<n>104:6</n> Semen Ábraham, servi ejus: * fílii Jacob, elécti ejus.
<n>104:7</n> Ipse Dóminus Deus noster: * in univérsa terra judícia ejus.
<n>104:8</n> Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * verbi, quod mandávit in mille generatiónes:
<n>104:9</n> Quod dispósuit ad Ábraham: * et juraménti sui ad Isaac:
<n>104:10</n> Et státuit illud Jacob in præcéptum: * et Israël in testaméntum ætérnum:
<n>104:11</n> Dicens: Tibi dabo terram Chánaan, * funículum hereditátis vestræ.
<n>104:12</n> Cum essent número brevi, * paucíssimi et íncolæ ejus:
<n>104:13</n> Et pertransiérunt de gente in gentem, * et de regno ad pópulum álterum.
<n>104:14</n> Non relíquit hóminem nocére eis: * et corrípuit pro eis reges.
<n>104:15</n> Nolíte tángere christos meos: * et in prophétis meis nolíte malignári.
<n>104:16</n> Et vocávit famem super terram: * et omne firmaméntum panis contrívit.
<n>104:17</n> Misit ante eos virum: * in servum venúmdatus est Joseph.
<n>104:18</n> Humiliavérunt in compédibus pedes ejus, ferrum pertránsiit ánimam ejus * donec veníret verbum ejus.
<n>104:19</n> Elóquium Dómini inflammávit eum: * misit rex, et solvit eum; princeps populórum, et dimísit eum.
<n>104:21</n> Constítuit eum dóminum domus suæ: * et príncipem omnis possessiónis suæ:
<n>104:22</n> Ut erudíret príncipes ejus sicut semetípsum: * et senes ejus prudéntiam docéret.
<n>104:23</n> Et intrávit Israël in Ægýptum: * et Jacob áccola fuit in terra Cham.
<n>104:24</n> Et auxit pópulum suum veheménter: * et firmávit eum super inimícos ejus.
<n>104:25</n> Convértit cor eórum ut odírent pópulum ejus: * et dolum fácerent in servos ejus.
<n>104:26</n> Misit Móysen, servum suum: * Aaron, quem elégit ipsum.
<n>104:27</n> Pósuit in eis verba signórum suórum: * et prodigiórum in terra Cham.
<n>104:28</n> Misit ténebras, et obscurávit: * et non exacerbávit sermónes suos.
<n>104:29</n> Convértit aquas eórum in sánguinem: * et occídit pisces eórum.
<n>104:30</n> Édidit terra eórum ranas: * in penetrálibus regum ipsórum.
<n>104:31</n> Dixit, et venit cœnomyía: * et cínifes in ómnibus fínibus eórum.
<n>104:32</n> Pósuit plúvias eórum grándinem: * ignem comburéntem in terra ipsórum.
<n>104:33</n> Et percússit víneas eórum, et ficúlneas eórum: * et contrívit lignum fínium eórum.
<n>104:34</n> Dixit, et venit locústa, et bruchus, * cujus non erat númerus:
<n>104:35</n> Et comédit omne fænum in terra eórum: * et comédit omnem fructum terræ eórum.
<n>104:36</n> Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra eórum: * primítias omnis labóris eórum.
<n>104:37</n> Et edúxit eos cum argénto et auro: * et non erat in tríbubus eórum infírmus.
<n>104:38</n> Lætáta est Ægýptus in profectióne eórum: * quia incúbuit timor eórum super eos.
<n>104:39</n> Expándit nubem in protectiónem eórum: * et ignem ut lucéret eis per noctem.
<n>104:40</n> Petiérunt, et venit cotúrnix: * et pane cæli saturávit eos.
<n>104:41</n> Dirúpit petram et fluxérunt aquæ: * abiérunt in sicco flúmina;
<n>104:42</n> Quóniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui: * quod hábuit ad Ábraham, púerum suum.
<n>104:43</n> Et edúxit pópulum suum in exsultatióne, * et eléctos suos in lætítia.
<n>104:44</n> Et dedit illis regiónes géntium: * et labóres populórum possedérunt:
<n>104:45</n> Ut custódiant justificatiónes ejus, * et legem ejus requírant.
10.L105:
<n>105:1</n> Confitémini Dómino, quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia ejus.
<n>105:2</n> Quis loquétur poténtias Dómini, * audítas fáciet omnes laudes ejus?
<n>105:3</n> Beáti, qui custódiunt judícium, * et fáciunt justítiam in omni témpore.
<n>105:4</n> Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui: * vísita nos in salutári tuo:
<n>105:5</n> Ad vidéndum in bonitáte electórum tuórum, ad lætándum in lætítia gentis tuæ: * ut laudéris cum hereditáte tua.
<n>105:6</n> Peccávimus cum pátribus nostris: * injúste égimus, iniquitátem fécimus.
<n>105:7</n> Patres nostri in Ægýpto non intellexérunt mirabília tua: * non fuérunt mémores multitúdinis misericórdiæ tuæ.
<n>105:7</n> Et irritavérunt ascendéntes in mare, * Mare Rubrum.
<n>105:8</n> Et salvávit eos propter nomen suum: * ut notam fáceret poténtiam suam.
<n>105:9</n> Et incrépuit Mare Rubrum, et exsiccátum est, * et dedúxit eos in abýssis sicut in desérto.
<n>105:10</n> Et salvávit eos de manu odiéntium: * et redémit eos de manu inimíci.
<n>105:11</n> Et opéruit aqua tribulántes eos: * unus ex eis non remánsit.
<n>105:12</n> Et credidérunt verbis ejus: * et laudavérunt laudem ejus.
<n>105:13</n> Cito fecérunt, oblíti sunt óperum ejus: * et non sustinuérunt consílium ejus.
<n>105:14</n> Et concupiérunt concupiscéntiam in desérto: * et tentavérunt Deum in inaquóso.
<n>105:15</n> Et dedit eis petitiónem ipsórum: * et misit saturitátem in ánimas eórum.
<n>105:16</n> Et irritavérunt Móysen in castris: * Aaron, sanctum Dómini.
<n>105:17</n> Apérta est terra, et deglutívit Dathan: * et opéruit super congregatiónem Abíron.
<n>105:18</n> Et exársit ignis in synagóga eórum * flamma combússit peccatóres.
<n>105:19</n> Et fecérunt vítulum in Horeb * et adoravérunt scúlptile.
<n>105:20</n> Et mutavérunt glóriam suam * in similitúdinem vítuli comedéntis fænum.
<n>105:21</n> Oblíti sunt Deum, qui salvávit eos, * qui fecit magnália in Ægýpto, mirabília in terra Cham: terribília in Mari Rubro.
<n>105:23</n> Et dixit ut dispérderet eos: * si non Móyses, eléctus ejus, stetísset in confractióne in conspéctu ejus:
<n>105:24</n> Ut avérteret iram ejus ne dispérderet eos: * et pro níhilo habuérunt terram desiderábilem:
<n>105:25</n> Non credidérunt verbo ejus, et murmuravérunt in tabernáculis suis: * non exaudiérunt vocem Dómini.
<n>105:26</n> Et elevávit manum suam super eos: * ut prostérneret eos in desérto:
<n>105:27</n> Et ut deíceret semen eórum in natiónibus: * et dispérgeret eos in regiónibus.
<n>105:28</n> Et initiáti sunt Beélphegor: * et comedérunt sacrifícia mortuórum.
<n>105:29</n> Et irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis: * et multiplicáta est in eis ruína.
<n>105:30</n> Et stetit Phínees, et placávit: * et cessávit quassátio.
<n>105:31</n> Et reputátum est ei in justítiam: * in generatiónem et generatiónem usque in sempitérnum.
<n>105:32</n> Et irritavérunt eum ad aquas contradictiónis: * et vexátus est Móyses propter eos: quia exacerbavérunt spíritum ejus.
<n>105:33</n> Et distínxit in lábiis suis: * non disperdidérunt gentes, quas dixit Dóminus illis.
<n>105:35</n> Et commísti sunt inter gentes, et didicérunt ópera eórum: et serviérunt sculptílibus eórum: * et factum est illis in scándalum.
<n>105:37</n> Et immolavérunt fílios suos, * et fílias suas dæmóniis.
<n>105:38</n> Et effudérunt sánguinem innocéntem: * sánguinem filiórum suórum et filiárum suárum, quas sacrificavérunt sculptílibus Chánaan.
<n>105:39</n> Et infécta est terra in sanguínibus, et contamináta est in opéribus eórum: * et fornicáti sunt in adinventiónibus suis.
<n>105:40</n> Et irátus est furóre Dóminus in pópulum suum: * et abominátus est hereditátem suam.
<n>105:41</n> Et trádidit eos in manus géntium: * et domináti sunt eórum qui odérunt eos.
<n>105:42</n> Et tribulavérunt eos inimíci eórum, et humiliáti sunt sub mánibus eórum: * sæpe liberávit eos.
<n>105:43</n> Ipsi autem exacerbavérunt eum in consílio suo: * et humiliáti sunt in iniquitátibus suis.
<n>105:44</n> Et vidit, cum tribularéntur: * et audívit oratiónem eórum.
<n>105:45</n> Et memor fuit testaménti sui: * et pœnítuit eum secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ suæ.
<n>105:46</n> Et dedit eos in misericórdias * in conspéctu ómnium qui céperant eos.
<n>105:47</n> Salvos nos fac, Dómine, Deus noster: * et cóngrega nos de natiónibus:
<n>105:47</n> Ut confiteámur nómini sancto tuo: * et gloriémur in laude tua.
<n>105:48</n> Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * et dicet omnis pópulus: Fiat, fiat.
10.L106:
<n>106:1</n> Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia ejus.
<n>106:2</n> Dicant qui redémpti sunt a Dómino, quos redémit de manu inimíci: * et de regiónibus congregávit eos:
<n>106:3</n> A solis ortu, et occásu: * ab aquilóne, et mari.
<n>106:4</n> Erravérunt in solitúdine in inaquóso: * viam civitátis habitáculi non invenérunt.
<n>106:5</n> Esuriéntes, et sitiéntes: * ánima eórum in ipsis defécit.
<n>106:6</n> Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum erípuit eos.
<n>106:7</n> Et dedúxit eos in viam rectam: * ut irent in civitátem habitatiónis.
<n>106:8</n> Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: * et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum.
<n>106:9</n> Quia satiávit ánimam inánem: * et ánimam esuriéntem satiávit bonis.
<n>106:10</n> Sedéntes in ténebris, et umbra mortis: * vinctos in mendicitáte et ferro.
<n>106:11</n> Quia exacerbavérunt elóquia Dei: * et consílium Altíssimi irritavérunt.
<n>106:12</n> Et humiliátum est in labóribus cor eórum: * infirmáti sunt, nec fuit qui adjuváret.
<n>106:13</n> Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
<n>106:14</n> Et edúxit eos de ténebris, et umbra mortis: * et víncula eórum disrúpit.
<n>106:15</n> Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: * et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum.
<n>106:16</n> Quia contrívit portas ǽreas: * et vectes férreos confrégit.
<n>106:17</n> Suscépit eos de via iniquitátis eórum: * propter injustítias enim suas humiliáti sunt.
<n>106:18</n> Omnem escam abomináta est ánima eórum: * et appropinquavérunt usque ad portas mortis.
<n>106:19</n> Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
<n>106:20</n> Misit verbum suum, et sanávit eos: * et erípuit eos de interitiónibus eórum.
<n>106:21</n> Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: * et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum.
<n>106:22</n> Et sacríficent sacrifícium laudis: * et annúntient ópera ejus in exsultatióne.
<n>106:23</n> Qui descéndunt mare in návibus, * faciéntes operatiónem in aquis multis.
<n>106:24</n> Ipsi vidérunt ópera Dómini, * et mirabília ejus in profúndo.
<n>106:25</n> Dixit, et stetit spíritus procéllæ: * et exaltáti sunt fluctus ejus.
<n>106:26</n> Ascéndunt usque ad cælos, et descéndunt usque ad abýssos: * ánima eórum in malis tabescébat.
<n>106:27</n> Turbáti sunt, et moti sunt sicut ébrius: * et omnis sapiéntia eórum devoráta est.
<n>106:28</n> Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum edúxit eos.
<n>106:29</n> Et státuit procéllam ejus in auram: * et siluérunt fluctus ejus.
<n>106:30</n> Et lætáti sunt quia siluérunt: * et dedúxit eos in portum voluntátis eórum.
<n>106:31</n> Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ ejus: * et mirabília ejus fíliis hóminum.
<n>106:32</n> Et exáltent eum in ecclésia plebis: * et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
<n>106:33</n> Pósuit flúmina in desértum: * et éxitus aquárum in sitim.
<n>106:34</n> Terram fructíferam in salsúginem: * a malítia inhabitántium in ea.
<n>106:35</n> Pósuit desértum in stagna aquárum: * et terram sine aqua in éxitus aquárum.
<n>106:36</n> Et collocávit illic esuriéntes: * et constituérunt civitátem habitatiónis.
<n>106:37</n> Et seminavérunt agros, et plantavérunt víneas: * et fecérunt fructum nativitátis.
<n>106:38</n> Et benedíxit eis, et multiplicáti sunt nimis: * et juménta eórum non minorávit.
<n>106:39</n> Et pauci facti sunt: * et vexáti sunt a tribulatióne malórum, et dolóre.
<n>106:40</n> Effúsa est contémptio super príncipes: * et erráre fecit eos in ínvio, et non in via.
<n>106:41</n> Et adjúvit páuperem de inópia: * et pósuit sicut oves famílias.
<n>106:42</n> Vidébunt recti, et lætabúntur: * et omnis iníquitas oppilábit os suum.
<n>106:43</n> Quis sápiens et custódiet hæc? * et intélleget misericórdias Dómini.
10.L107:
<n>107:2</n> Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psallam in glória mea.
<n>107:3</n> Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
<n>107:4</n> Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psallam tibi in natiónibus.
<n>107:5</n> Quia magna est super cælos misericórdia tua: * et usque ad nubes véritas tua:
<n>107:6</n> Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.
<n>107:7</n> Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:
<n>107:8</n> Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.
<n>107:9</n> Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.
<n>107:10</n> Juda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.
<n>107:10</n> In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.
<n>107:11</n> Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
<n>107:12</n> Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
<n>107:13</n> Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
<n>107:14</n> In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet inimícos nostros.
10.L108:
<n>108:2</n> Deus, laudem meam ne tacúeris: * quia os peccatóris, et os dolósi super me apértum est.
<n>108:3</n> Locúti sunt advérsum me lingua dolósa, et sermónibus ódii circumdedérunt me: * et expugnavérunt me gratis.
<n>108:4</n> Pro eo ut me dilígerent, detrahébant mihi: * ego autem orábam.
<n>108:5</n> Et posuérunt advérsum me mala pro bonis: * et ódium pro dilectióne mea.
<n>108:6</n> Constítue super eum peccatórem: * et diábolus stet a dextris ejus.
<n>108:7</n> Cum judicátur, éxeat condemnátus: * et orátio ejus fiat in peccátum.
<n>108:8</n> Fiant dies ejus pauci: * et episcopátum ejus accípiat alter.
<n>108:9</n> Fiant fílii ejus órphani: * et uxor ejus vídua.
<n>108:10</n> Nutántes transferántur fílii ejus, et mendícent: * et eiciántur de habitatiónibus suis.
<n>108:11</n> Scrutétur fænerátor omnem substántiam ejus: * et dirípiant aliéni labóres ejus.
<n>108:12</n> Non sit illi adjútor: * nec sit qui misereátur pupíllis ejus.
<n>108:13</n> Fiant nati ejus in intéritum: * in generatióne una deleátur nomen ejus.
<n>108:14</n> In memóriam rédeat iníquitas patrum ejus in conspéctu Dómini: * et peccátum matris ejus non deleátur.
<n>108:15</n> Fiant contra Dóminum semper, et dispéreat de terra memória eórum: * pro eo quod non est recordátus fácere misericórdiam.
<n>108:17</n> Et persecútus est hóminem ínopem, et mendícum, * et compúnctum corde mortificáre.
<n>108:18</n> Et diléxit maledictiónem, et véniet ei: * et nóluit benedictiónem, et elongábitur ab eo.
<n>108:18</n> Et índuit maledictiónem sicut vestiméntum, * et intrávit sicut aqua in interióra ejus, et sicut óleum in óssibus ejus.
<n>108:19</n> Fiat ei sicut vestiméntum, quo operítur: * et sicut zona, qua semper præcíngitur.
<n>108:20</n> Hoc opus eórum, qui détrahunt mihi apud Dóminum: * et qui loquúntur mala advérsus ánimam meam.
<n>108:21</n> Et tu, Dómine, Dómine, fac mecum propter nomen tuum: * quia suávis est misericórdia tua.
<n>108:22</n> Líbera me quia egénus, et pauper ego sum: * et cor meum conturbátum est intra me.
<n>108:23</n> Sicut umbra cum declínat, ablátus sum: * et excússus sum sicut locústæ.
<n>108:24</n> Génua mea infirmáta sunt a jejúnio: * et caro mea immutáta est propter óleum.
<n>108:25</n> Et ego factus sum oppróbrium illis: * vidérunt me, et movérunt cápita sua.
<n>108:26</n> Ádjuva me, Dómine, Deus meus: * salvum me fac secúndum misericórdiam tuam.
<n>108:27</n> Et sciant quia manus tua hæc: * et tu, Dómine, fecísti eam.
<n>108:28</n> Maledícent illi, et tu benedíces: * qui insúrgunt in me, confundántur: servus autem tuus lætábitur.
<n>108:29</n> Induántur qui détrahunt mihi, pudóre: * et operiántur sicut diplóide confusióne sua.
<n>108:30</n> Confitébor Dómino nimis in ore meo: * et in médio multórum laudábo eum.
<n>108:31</n> Quia ástitit a dextris páuperis, * ut salvam fáceret a persequéntibus ánimam meam.
10.E100:
<n>100:1</n> Mercy and judgment * I will sing to thee, O Lord:
<n>100:2</n> I will sing, and I will understand in the unspotted way, * when thou shalt come to me.
<n>100:2</n> I walked in the innocence of my heart, * in the midst of my house.
<n>100:3</n> I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: * I hated the workers of iniquities.
<n>100:4</n> The perverse heart did not cleave to me: * and the malignant, that turned aside from me, I would not know.
<n>100:5</n> The man that in private detracted his neighbour, * him did I persecute.
<n>100:5</n> With him that had a proud eye, and an unsatiable heart, * I would not eat.
<n>100:6</n> My eyes were upon the faithful of the earth, to sit with me: * the man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.
<n>100:7</n> He that worketh pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: * he that speaketh unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.
<n>100:8</n> In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: * that I might cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.
10.E101:
<n>101:2</n> Hear, O Lord, my prayer: * and let my cry come to thee.
<n>101:3</n> Turn not away thy face from me: * in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me.
<n>101:3</n> In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * hear me speedily.
<n>101:4</n> For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.
<n>101:5</n> I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.
<n>101:6</n> Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.
<n>101:7</n> I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.
<n>101:8</n> I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.
<n>101:9</n> All the day long my enemies reproached me: * and they that praised me did swear against me.
<n>101:10</n> For I did eat ashes like bread, * and mingled my drink with weeping.
<n>101:11</n> Because of thy anger and indignation: * for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.
<n>101:12</n> My days have declined like a shadow, * and I am withered like grass.
<n>101:13</n> But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever: * and thy memorial to all generations.
<n>101:14</n> Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: * for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come.
<n>101:15</n> For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants: * and they shall have pity on the earth thereof.
<n>101:16</n> And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth thy glory.
<n>101:17</n> For the Lord hath built up Sion: * and he shall be seen in his glory.
<n>101:18</n> He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble: * and he hath not despised their petition.
<n>101:19</n> Let these things be written unto another generation: * and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:
<n>101:20</n> Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary: * from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth.
<n>101:21</n> That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters: * that he might release the children of the slain:
<n>101:22</n> That they may declare the name of the Lord in Sion: * and his praise in Jerusalem;
<n>101:23</n> When the people assemble together, * and kings, to serve the Lord.
<n>101:24</n> He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.
<n>101:25</n> Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.
<n>101:26</n> In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.
<n>101:27</n> They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:
<n>101:28</n> And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.
<n>101:29</n> The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.
10.E102:
<n>102:1</n> Bless the Lord, O my soul: * and let all that is within me bless his holy name.
<n>102:2</n> Bless the Lord, O my soul, * and never forget all he hath done for thee.
<n>102:3</n> Who forgiveth all thy iniquities: * who healeth all thy diseases.
<n>102:4</n> Who redeemeth thy life from destruction: * who crowneth thee with mercy and compassion.
<n>102:5</n> Who satisfieth thy desire with good things: * thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s.
<n>102:6</n> The Lord doth mercies, * and judgment for all that suffer wrong.
<n>102:7</n> He hath made his ways known to Moses: * his wills to the children of Israel.
<n>102:8</n> The Lord is compassionate and merciful: * longsuffering and plenteous in mercy.
<n>102:9</n> He will not always be angry: * nor will he threaten for ever.
<n>102:10</n> He hath not dealt with us according to our sins: * nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.
<n>102:11</n> For according to the height of the heaven above the earth: * he hath strengthened his mercy towards them that fear him.
<n>102:12</n> As far as the east is from the west, * so far hath he removed our iniquities from us.
<n>102:13</n> As a father hath compassion on his children, so hath the Lord compassion on them that fear him: * for he knoweth our frame.
<n>102:14</n> He remembereth that we are dust: * man’s days are as grass, as the flower of the field so shall he flourish.
<n>102:16</n> For the spirit shall pass in him, and he shall not be: * and he shall know his place no more.
<n>102:17</n> But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity * and unto eternity upon them that fear him:
<n>102:17</n> And his justice unto children’s children, * to such as keep his covenant,
<n>102:18</n> And are mindful of his commandments * to do them.
<n>102:19</n> The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven: * and his kingdom shall rule over all.
<n>102:20</n> Bless the Lord, all ye his angels: * you that are mighty in strength, and execute his word, hearkening to the voice of his orders.
<n>102:21</n> Bless the Lord, all ye his hosts: * you ministers of his that do his will.
<n>102:22</n> Bless the Lord, all his works: * in every place of his dominion, O my soul, bless thou the Lord.
10.E103:
<n>103:1</n> Bless the Lord, O my soul: * O Lord my God, thou art exceedingly great.
<n>103:1</n> Thou hast put on praise and beauty: * and art clothed with light as with a garment.
<n>103:2</n> Who stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion: * who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water.
<n>103:3</n> Who makest the clouds thy chariot: * who walkest upon the wings of the winds.
<n>103:4</n> Who makest thy angels spirits: * and thy ministers a burning fire.
<n>103:5</n> Who hast founded the earth upon its own bases: * it shall not be moved for ever and ever.
<n>103:6</n> The deep like a garment is its clothing: * above the mountains shall the waters stand.
<n>103:7</n> At thy rebuke they shall flee: * at the voice of thy thunder they shall fear.
<n>103:8</n> The mountains ascend, and the plains descend * into the place which thou hast founded for them.
<n>103:9</n> Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass over; * neither shall they return to cover the earth.
<n>103:10</n> Thou sendest forth springs in the vales: * between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass.
<n>103:11</n> All the beasts of the field shall drink: * the wild asses shall expect in their thirst.
<n>103:12</n> Over them the birds of the air shall dwell: * from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices.
<n>103:13</n> Thou waterest the hills from thy upper rooms: * the earth shall be filled with the fruit of thy works:
<n>103:14</n> Bringing forth grass for cattle, * and herb for the service of men.
<n>103:14</n> That thou mayst bring bread out of the earth: * and that wine may cheer the heart of man.
<n>103:15</n> That he may make the face cheerful with oil: * and that bread may strengthen man’s heart.
<n>103:16</n> The trees of the field shall be filled, and the cedars of Libanus which he hath planted: * there the sparrows shall make their nests.
<n>103:17</n> The highest of them is the house of the heron. * The high hills are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins.
<n>103:19</n> He hath made the moon for seasons: * the sun knoweth his going down.
<n>103:20</n> Thou hast appointed darkness, and it is night: * in it shall all the beasts of the woods go about:
<n>103:21</n> The young lions roaring after their prey, * and seeking their meat from God.
<n>103:22</n> The sun ariseth, and they are gathered together: * and they shall lie down in their dens.
<n>103:23</n> Man shall go forth to his work, * and to his labour until the evening.
<n>103:24</n> How great are thy works, O Lord? * thou hast made all things in wisdom: the earth is filled with thy riches.
<n>103:25</n> So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms: * there are creeping things without number:
<n>103:26</n> Creatures little and great. * There the ships shall go.
<n>103:27</n> This sea dragon which thou hast formed to play therein. * All expect of thee that thou give them food in season.
<n>103:28</n> What thou givest to them they shall gather up: * when thou openest thy hand, they shall all be filled with good.
<n>103:29</n> But if thou turnest away thy face, they shall be troubled: * thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall return to their dust.
<n>103:30</n> Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created: * and thou shalt renew the face of the earth.
<n>103:31</n> May the glory of the Lord endure for ever: * the Lord shall rejoice in his works.
<n>103:32</n> He looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble: * he toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.
<n>103:33</n> I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: * I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
<n>103:34</n> Let my speech be acceptable to him: * but I will take delight in the Lord.
<n>103:35</n> Let sinners be consumed out of the earth, and the unjust, so that they be no more: * O my soul, bless thou the Lord.
10.E104:
<n>104:1</n> Give glory to the Lord, and call upon his name: * declare his deeds among the Gentiles.
<n>104:2</n> Sing to him, yea sing praises to him: * relate all his wondrous works.
<n>104:3</n> Glory ye in his holy name: * let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.
<n>104:4</n> Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened: * seek his face evermore.
<n>104:5</n> Remember his marvellous works which he hath done; * his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth.
<n>104:6</n> O ye seed of Abraham his servant; * ye sons of Jacob his chosen.
<n>104:7</n> He is the Lord our God: * his judgments are in all the earth.
<n>104:8</n> He hath remembered his covenant for ever: * the word which he commanded to a thousand generations.
<n>104:9</n> Which he made to Abraham; * and his oath to Isaac:
<n>104:10</n> And he appointed the same to Jacob for a law, * and to Israel for an everlasting testament:
<n>104:11</n> Saying: To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, * the lot of your inheritance.
<n>104:12</n> When they were but a small number: * yea very few, and sojourners therein:
<n>104:13</n> And they passed from nation to nation, * and from one kingdom to another people.
<n>104:14</n> He suffered no man to hurt them: * and he reproved kings for their sakes.
<n>104:15</n> Touch ye not my anointed: * and do no evil to my prophets.
<n>104:16</n> And he called a famine upon the land: * and he broke in pieces all the support of bread.
<n>104:17</n> He sent a man before them: * Joseph, who was sold for a slave.
<n>104:18</n> They humbled his feet in fetters: the iron pierced his soul, * until his word came.
<n>104:19</n> The word of the Lord inflamed him: * the king sent, and he released him: the ruler of the people, and he set him at liberty.
<n>104:21</n> He made him master of his house, * and ruler of all his possession.
<n>104:22</n> That he might instruct his princes as himself, * and teach his ancients wisdom.
<n>104:23</n> And Israel went into Egypt: * and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Cham.
<n>104:24</n> And he increased his people exceedingly: * and strengthened them over their enemies,
<n>104:25</n> He turned their heart to hate his people: * and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
<n>104:26</n> He sent Moses his servant: * Aaron the man whom he had chosen.
<n>104:27</n> He gave them power to shew his signs, * and his wonders in the land of Cham.
<n>104:28</n> He sent darkness, and made it obscure: * and grieved not his words.
<n>104:29</n> He turned their waters into blood, * and destroyed their fish.
<n>104:30</n> Their land brought forth frogs, * in the inner chambers of their kings.
<n>104:31</n> He spoke, and there came diverse sorts of flies, * and sciniphs in all their coasts.
<n>104:32</n> He gave them hail for rain, * a burning fire in the land.
<n>104:33</n> And he destroyed their vineyards, and their fig trees: * and he broke in pieces the trees of their coasts.
<n>104:34</n> He spoke, and the locust came, and the bruchus, * of which there was no number.
<n>104:35</n> And they devoured all the grass in their land, * and consumed all the fruit of their ground.
<n>104:36</n> And he slew all the firstborn in their land: * the firstfruits of all their labour.
<n>104:37</n> And he brought them out with silver and gold: * and there was not among their tribes one that was feeble.
<n>104:38</n> Egypt was glad when they departed: * for the fear of them lay upon them.
<n>104:39</n> He spread a cloud for their protection, * and fire to give them light in the night.
<n>104:40</n> They asked, and the quail came: * and he filled them with the bread of heaven.
<n>104:41</n> He opened the rock, and waters flowed: * rivers ran down in the dry land.
<n>104:42</n> Because he remembered his holy word, * which he had spoken to his servant Abraham.
<n>104:43</n> And he brought forth his people with joy, * and his chosen with gladness.
<n>104:44</n> And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles: * and they possessed the labours of the people:
<n>104:45</n> That they might observe his justifications, * and seek after his law.
10.E105:
<n>105:1</n> Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>105:2</n> Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? * who shall set forth all his praises?
<n>105:3</n> Blessed are they that keep judgment, * and do justice at all times.
<n>105:4</n> Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people: * visit us with thy salvation.
<n>105:5</n> That we may see the good of thy chosen, that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation: * that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance.
<n>105:6</n> We have sinned with our fathers: * we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.
<n>105:7</n> Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt: * they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies:
<n>105:7</n> And they provoked to wrath going up to the sea, * even the Red Sea.
<n>105:8</n> And he saved them for his own name’s sake: * that he might make his power known.
<n>105:9</n> And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up: * and he led them through the depths, as in a wilderness.
<n>105:10</n> And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them: * and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
<n>105:11</n> And the water covered them that afflicted them: * there was not one of them left.
<n>105:12</n> And they believed his words: * and they sang his praises.
<n>105:13</n> They had quickly done, they forgot his works: * and they waited not for his counsels.
<n>105:14</n> And they coveted their desire in the desert: * and they tempted God in the place without water.
<n>105:15</n> And he gave them their request: * and sent fulness into their souls.
<n>105:16</n> And they provoked Moses in the camp, * Aaron the holy one of the Lord.
<n>105:17</n> The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan: * and covered the congregation of Abiron.
<n>105:18</n> And a fire was kindled in their congregation: * the flame burned the wicked.
<n>105:19</n> They made also a calf in Horeb: * and they adored the graven thing.
<n>105:20</n> And they changed their glory * into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass.
<n>105:21</n> They forgot God, who saved them, * who had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Cham: terrible things in the Red Sea.
<n>105:23</n> And he said that he would destroy them: * had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach:
<n>105:24</n> To turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them; * and they set at nought the desirable land.
<n>105:25</n> They believed not his word, and they murmured in their tents: * they hearkened not to the voice of the Lord.
<n>105:26</n> And he lifted up his hand over them: * to overthrow them in the desert;
<n>105:27</n> And to cast down their seed among the nations, * and to scatter them in the countries.
<n>105:28</n> They also were initiated to Beelphegor: * and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
<n>105:29</n> And they provoked him with their inventions: * and destruction was multiplied among them.
<n>105:30</n> Then Phinees stood up, and pacified him: * and the slaughter ceased.
<n>105:31</n> And it was reputed to him unto justice, * to generation and generation for evermore.
<n>105:32</n> They provoked him also at the waters of contradiction: * and Moses was afflicted for their sakes: because they exasperated his spirit.
<n>105:33</n> And he distinguished with his lips; * they did not destroy the nations of which the Lord spoke unto them.
<n>105:35</n> And they were mingled among the heathens, and learned their works: and served their idols, * and it became a stumblingblock to them.
<n>105:37</n> And they sacrificed their sons, * and their daughters to devils.
<n>105:38</n> And they shed innocent blood: * the blood of their sons and of their daughters which they sacrificed to the idols of Chanaan.
<n>105:39</n> And the land was polluted with blood, and was defiled with their works: * and they went aside after their own inventions.
<n>105:40</n> And the Lord was exceedingly angry with his people: * and he abhorred his inheritance.
<n>105:41</n> And he delivered them into the hands of the nations: * and they that hated them had dominion over them.
<n>105:42</n> And their enemies afflicted them: and they were humbled under their hands: * many times did he deliver them.
<n>105:43</n> But they provoked him with their counsel: * and they were brought low by their iniquities.
<n>105:44</n> And he saw when they were in tribulation: * and he heard their prayer.
<n>105:45</n> And he was mindful of his covenant: * and repented according to the multitude of his mercies.
<n>105:46</n> And he gave them unto mercies, * in the sight of all those that had made them captives.
<n>105:47</n> Save us, O Lord, our God: * and gather us from among nations:
<n>105:47</n> That we may give thanks to thy holy name, * and may glory in thy praise.
<n>105:48</n> Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting: * and let all the people say: So be it, so be it.
10.E106:
<n>106:1</n> Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>106:2</n> Let them say so that have been redeemed by the Lord, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy: * and gathered out of the countries.
<n>106:3</n> From the rising and the setting of the sun, * from the north and from the sea.
<n>106:4</n> They wandered in a wilderness, in a place without water: * they found not the way of a city for their habitation.
<n>106:5</n> They were hungry and thirsty: * their soul fainted in them.
<n>106:6</n> And they cried to the Lord in their tribulation: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
<n>106:7</n> And he led them into the right way: * that they might go to a city of habitation.
<n>106:8</n> Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
<n>106:9</n> For he hath satisfied the empty soul, * and hath filled the hungry soul with good things.
<n>106:10</n> Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death: * bound in want and in iron.
<n>106:11</n> Because they had exasperated the words of God: * and provoked the counsel of the most High:
<n>106:12</n> And their heart was humbled with labours: * they were weakened, and there was none to help them.
<n>106:13</n> Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
<n>106:14</n> And he brought them out of darkness, * and the shadow of death; and broke their bonds in sunder.
<n>106:15</n> Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
<n>106:16</n> Because he hath broken gates of brass, * and burst the iron bars.
<n>106:17</n> He took them out of the way of their iniquity: * for they were brought low for their injustices.
<n>106:18</n> Their soul abhorred all manner of meat: * and they drew nigh even to the gates of death.
<n>106:19</n> And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.
<n>106:20</n> He sent his word, and healed them: * and delivered them from their destructions.
<n>106:21</n> Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
<n>106:22</n> And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise: * and declare his works with joy.
<n>106:23</n> They that go down to the sea in ships, * doing business in the great waters:
<n>106:24</n> These have seen the works of the Lord, * and his wonders in the deep.
<n>106:25</n> He said the word, and there arose a storm of wind: * and the waves thereof were lifted up.
<n>106:26</n> They mount up to the heavens, and they go down to the depths: * their soul pined away with evils.
<n>106:27</n> They were troubled, and reeled like a drunken man; * and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
<n>106:28</n> And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he brought them out of their distresses.
<n>106:29</n> And he turned the storm into a breeze: * and its waves were still.
<n>106:30</n> And they rejoiced because they were still: * and he brought them to the haven which they wished for.
<n>106:31</n> Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.
<n>106:32</n> And let them exalt him in the church of the people: * and praise him in the chair of the ancients.
<n>106:33</n> He hath turned rivers into a wilderness: * and the sources of water into dry ground:
<n>106:34</n> A fruitful land into barrenness, * for the wickedness of them that dwell therein.
<n>106:35</n> He hath turned a wilderness into pools of water, * and a dry land into water springs.
<n>106:36</n> And hath placed there the hungry; * and they made a city for their habitation.
<n>106:37</n> And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards: * and they yielded fruit of birth.
<n>106:38</n> And he blessed them, and they were multiplied exceedingly: * and their cattle he suffered not to decrease.
<n>106:39</n> Then they were brought to be few: * and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils and sorrow.
<n>106:40</n> Contempt was poured forth upon their princes: * and he caused them to wander where there was no passing, and out of the way.
<n>106:41</n> And he helped the poor out of poverty: * and made him families like a flock of sheep.
<n>106:42</n> The just shall see, and shall rejoice, * and all iniquity shall stop their mouth.
<n>106:43</n> Who is wise, and will keep these things: * and will understand the mercies of the Lord?
10.E107:
<n>107:2</n> My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and will give praise, with my glory.
<n>107:3</n> Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp * I will arise in the morning early.
<n>107:4</n> I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: * and I will sing unto thee among the nations.
<n>107:5</n> For thy mercy is great above the heavens: * and thy truth even unto the clouds.
<n>107:6</n> Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth: * that thy beloved may be delivered.
<n>107:7</n> Save with thy right hand and hear me. * God hath spoken in his holiness.
<n>107:8</n> I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem * and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
<n>107:9</n> Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim the protection of my head.
<n>107:10</n> Juda is my king: * Moab the pot of my hope.
<n>107:10</n> Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: * the aliens are become my friends.
<n>107:11</n> Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?
<n>107:12</n> Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?
<n>107:13</n> O grant us help from trouble: * for vain is the help of man.
<n>107:14</n> Through God we shall do mightily: * and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
10.E108:
<n>108:2</n> God, be not thou silent in my praise: * for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me.
<n>108:3</n> They have spoken against me with deceitful tongues; and they have compassed me about with words of hatred; * and have fought against me without cause.
<n>108:4</n> Instead of making me a return of love, they detracted me: * but I gave myself to prayer.
<n>108:5</n> And they repaid me evil for good: * and hatred for my love.
<n>108:6</n> Set thou the sinner over him: * and may the devil stand at his right hand.
<n>108:7</n> When he is judged, may he go out condemned; * and may his prayer be turned to sin.
<n>108:8</n> May his days be few: * and his bishopric let another take.
<n>108:9</n> May his children be fatherless, * and his wife a widow.
<n>108:10</n> Let his children be carried about vagabonds, and beg; * and let them be cast out of their dwellings.
<n>108:11</n> May the usurer search all his substance: * and let strangers plunder his labours.
<n>108:12</n> May there be none to help him: * nor none to pity his fatherless offspring.
<n>108:13</n> May his posterity be cut off; * in one generation may his name be blotted out.
<n>108:14</n> May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered in the sight of the Lord: * and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
<n>108:15</n> May they be before the Lord continually, and let the memory of them perish from the earth: * because he remembered not to shew mercy,
<n>108:17</n> But persecuted the poor man and the beggar; * and the broken in heart, to put him to death.
<n>108:18</n> And he loved cursing, and it shall come unto him: * and he would not have blessing, and it shall be far from him.
<n>108:18</n> And he put on cursing, like a garment: * and it went in like water into his entrails, and like oil in his bones.
<n>108:19</n> May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him; * and like a girdle with which he is girded continually.
<n>108:20</n> This is the work of them who detract me before the Lord; * and who speak evils against my soul.
<n>108:21</n> But thou, O Lord, do with me for thy name’s sake: * because thy mercy is sweet.
<n>108:22</n> Do thou deliver me, for I am poor and needy, * and my heart is troubled within me.
<n>108:23</n> I am taken away like the shadow when it declineth: * and I am shaken off as locusts.
<n>108:24</n> My knees are weakened through fasting: * and my flesh is changed for oil.
<n>108:25</n> And I am become a reproach to them: * they saw me and they shaked their heads.
<n>108:26</n> Help me, O Lord my God; * save me according to thy mercy.
<n>108:27</n> And let them know that this is thy hand: * and that thou, O Lord, hast done it.
<n>108:28</n> They will curse and thou wilt bless: * let them that rise up against me be confounded: but thy servant shall rejoice.
<n>108:29</n> Let them that detract me be clothed with shame: * and let them be covered with their confusion as with a double cloak.
<n>108:30</n> I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: * and in the midst of many I will praise him.
<n>108:31</n> Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor, * to save my soul from persecutors.
